# SmolVLA stage totals

<!-- generated by `python -m workload_modeling.build`; do not edit by hand -->

Per-stage compute and memory needs of one SmolVLA policy call, from the standalone model (`infra/workload-modeling/`). The model follows the reference computation (lerobot SmolVLA code) at true token counts; its matrix-product FLOP agree with PR1's compiled programs within 0.011 % once PR1's padding and rewrites are applied ([crosscheck.md](crosscheck.md)). Label: inference (model output), cross-checked.

Conventions ([conventions.md](conventions.md)): fp16 (2 B per element); `bytes_weight` re-reads each layer's weights once per call and the expert's weights once per flow step; `bytes_unique` adds each operator's inputs and outputs; FLOP per weight byte = FLOP / `bytes_weight`. Non-matrix FLOP use per-element conventions.

## Reading against a machine balance

A stage whose FLOP per weight byte is below a machine's peak FLOP/s divided by its memory bandwidth is limited by streaming weights at batch size 1, if weights cannot stay on chip. For Jetson Thor that balance is `thor.fp16_dense` / `thor.dram_bw` = 945 FLOP per byte (inference). The SoftHier balance depends on the HBM bandwidth, which is an open parameter ([hw-config.md](hw-config.md)).
